about.title: About {site}
about.metaDescription: About {site}: free, open-source desktop software for biologists.

blocks.text: {site} is a collection of free, open-source desktop apps for biological research.
Good tools save scientists time. When tools are open and free, rather than behind commercial licences, we can all build on each other's work.

items.text: Each has its own page with an overview, requirements and a download link to the latest release.
Software from other groups that I use, with links to each project's website and source code.

blocks.text: This is a short, personal list, not a full index. A tool is listed only if:

items: I use it in my own work.
It is free, with no registration or licence request.
It has an easy-to-use graphical interface, on desktop or in the browser.
It runs on your computer without needing the internet.

blocks.text: Most are open source. A few are free but not open source: UCSF ChimeraX is free for academic use, Obsidian is free for personal use, and Visual Studio Code's source is MIT-licensed but Microsoft's builds have their own licence. Each entry's licence badge shows exactly what you get.
I am not affiliated with these projects. Links go to each project's own website, so you always download from the developers. Names and trademarks belong to their owners.
This site is a public repository. To report a broken link or a wrong description, or to suggest a tool, open an issue or send a pull request.
